retraction.summary: The prior pass's site (29.456,-97.750, 'high' confidence, 'grading since 2026-01/02') is WRONG for this project. That footprint is Hoke Solar (23INR0231, f/k/a Brush Country Solar), a 95.29 MW project on a different 138kV tap (Deer Creek-Nixon) in Gonzales County. See research/23INR0231_hoke-solar/sources/SITE_DERIVATION.md.
how_the_error_happened: The 2026-07-20 deep pass correctly identified that the EIA-860M coordinate (29.26357,-97.78055) used in the FIRST triage/deep pass was actually the town centroid of Nixon, TX, not the plant -- a real and useful catch.

It then tried to re-derive the site with a 15km AWS Open Data sweep 'due east' of Elm Creek substation (29.4673,-97.99988), per the IA's '18.5 mi East of Elm Creek station' language, and found A large graded/cleared multi-block site ~15 mi out and adopted it (29.456,-97.750).

That site is real construction -- it is just not THIS project's. It belongs to Hoke Solar (23INR0231), confirmed independently via: FCC census geocode = Gonzales County (not Wilson, the queue county for Cachena); the only OSM transmission line within 2km of that footprint is 138kV (not the 345kV Elm Creek-STP circuit Cachena/Clear Fork interconnects to); the footprint's ~550-acre scale fits Hoke's 95.29 MW, not Cachena's 602 MW / 4,600-acre project; and Hoke's own Ch.313 application boundary map (scale-bar-derived georeference) lands dead-center on that same footprint.

The 'visually confirmed construction matching developer's own timeline' claim in the prior findings.json was circular: Enbridge's own public project-updates page states ONLY that site prep began Aug 2025 and construction began Q4 2025 -- it gives NO location detail (checked both sources/2026-07-19_enbridge_clear-fork-solar-project-updates.html and the FAQ). The prior pass found *a* construction site matching that rough date order at a plausible-looking bearing/distance and treated the coincidence as confirmation, without checking county, voltage, or an independent boundary map -- the same class of miss as the EIA-town-centroid bug it had just caught.

SITE_CORROBORATION_tceq.md (2026-07-20) separately surfaced a real address (10046 US Highway 87 East, Wilson County -- see below) but mis-read it as merely corroborating the Nixon-centroid EIA point (29.26357,-97.78055) rather than geocoding it as an independent site fix in its own right.

site.method: RE-DERIVED 2026-07-21 from the project's OWN regulatory address, not imagery. TCEQ Central Registry construction-stormwater NOIs (sources/2026-07-20_tceq_stormwater_nois_clearfork_cachena.json) list THREE related active registrations sharing the physical address '10046 US Highway 87 East / US Hwy 87 E', Wilson County: 'CLEAR FORK CREEK SOLAR' (the generation facility itself, TXR1512VO, active since 2025-08-15, owner/EPC Hanwha Q Cells EPC USA LLC), 'CLEAR FORK CREEK SOLAR SUBSTATION' (TXR1573TG, since 2025-01-13, same EPC), and 'CACHENA SOLAR POI' (TXR1599VD, since 2025-07-09, owner Dorazio Enterprises, described as 'CPS ENERGY SOLAR POI'). This address was geocoded independently by TWO separate services: Esri/ArcGIS World Geocoder (score 100, StreetAddress match, AddNum 10046 in range 9900-10326) -> 29.257169,-97.809055, 'Nixon, TX 78140'; and Google Places API (street_address type) -> 29.258670,-97.802252, 'Stockdale, TX 78160' (rural US-87 addressing straddles both postal cities). The two independent geocodes agree to within ~0.5 mi; adopted point is their average. CORROBORATION 2026-07-21: the 2025-07-14 Wilson County agenda defines the Clear Fork Creek Solar Reinvestment Zone as ~6,100 ac straddling Hwy 87 in Precinct 4 — consistent with the 10046 US Hwy 87 E address anchor (29.2579,-97.8057). Parcel IDs available for future CAD boundary lookup.
site.confidence: medium -- two independent commercial geocoders converge on the project's own registered construction-site address (not a third-party aggregator or a town centroid), and the straight-line distance from Elm Creek substation (29.4673,-97.99988) to this point is 18.57 mi, within 0.4% of the IA's stated 'approximately 18.5 miles East' POI language (bearing is ESE, not due-east, but the IA text is a rough narrative description, not a bearing spec). However: no parcel/CAD boundary map exists to pin the array's actual perimeter (Ch.312/Ch.313/JETI checked, all negative -- see below), and a ~24km x 24km Sentinel-2 sweep centered here shows NO visible large-scale grading (see construction, below) -- so this is a well-sourced ENTRANCE/address anchor for the project, not an imagery-confirmed array footprint.
cross_checks: TCEQ stormwater NOIs (sources/2026-07-20_tceq_stormwater_nois_clearfork_cachena.json): all three related registrations (main array, substation, POI) share address '10046 US Highway 87 East', Wilson County
Google Places API: 29.258670,-97.802252 (street_address) -- independent second geocoder, agrees to ~0.5 mi
Distance check: 18.57 mi from Elm Creek substation vs. IA's stated ~18.5 mi (0.4% delta)

EIA-860M 'Clear Fork Creek Solar and BESS SLF' point (29.26357,-97.78055) -- this is the Nixon, TX town centroid (confirmed by dense street grid at that exact point in imagery; an administrative/reporting artifact, NOT the plant) -- sits only ~1.5 mi from the newly-derived address point, i.e. it is a loose corroborating anchor (same neighborhood) but was WRONGLY treated as a primary site fix in the 2026-07-20 pass

Ch.312 resolve (ch312.py, 2026-07-21): 2 Wilson County candidates, both 'City of La Vernia Crossing Reinvestment Zone' -- unrelated commercial development, NOT Clear Fork Creek Solar. No boundary map available from this rung.
Ch.313 resolve (ch313.py, 2026-07-21): NEGATIVE -- no Ch.313 agreement or JETI application for 'Cachena Solar SLF' (expected; program expired 2022, project took FID without value-limitation filing)
data/reference/ch312_abatements_detail.csv and ch313_agreements.json grepped for 'clear fork'/'cachena': no hits

Hoke Solar's SITE_DERIVATION.md georeference (29.453,-97.751, Ch.313 boundary map) is ~14.4 mi NORTH of this point -- confirms the two projects are genuinely distinct, well-separated sites, not the same footprint viewed two ways

project_area.source: Enbridge FAQ: 'Clear Fork spans approximately 4,600 acres of privately owned land'

notes: RETRACTED 2026-07-21: the prior 6-date 'grading_active' timeline (2024-06 through 2026-06, showing a site graded into ~6 rectangular blocks by 2026-06-29) was observed at 29.456,-97.750 -- Hoke Solar's (23INR0231) footprint, not this project's. That imagery has been deleted from imagery/key/.

New imagery fetched 2026-07-21 at the re-derived true-site address anchor (29.2579,-97.8057), 3km buffer, 5 dates spanning the same window: 2024-06-09 (19.2% cloud, partial coverage but visible portions show unbroken agricultural/ranch land, no clearing), 2025-06-17 (0.5% cloud, agricultural land with center-pivot irrigation, a small pre-existing tank/utility yard along US-87 -- present and unchanged in ALL frames including the 2024 baseline, so it predates this project and is not new construction), 2025-11-26 (5.2% cloud, same, no clearing), 2026-05-03 (0.1% cloud, same, no clearing), 2026-07-09 (4.3% cloud, same, no clearing). NONE of the five dates shows any grading, racking rows, or large-scale earthwork.

Widened the search to rule out a nearby offset: single-scene sweeps at 6km, 14km x 24km (undistorted), and 15km buffer around the address point, plus a second 18km x 24km tile shifted north toward Clear Fork Creek itself -- roughly 24km x 24km total coverage, most recent low-cloud scene (2026-07-09, 4.3% cloud). The only large disturbed-earth feature found in that area is an irregular ~1 km blob with internal haul roads and standing-water ponds south of the address point -- consistent with a pre-existing aggregate/caliche quarry, not a 4,600-acre utility-scale solar array (wrong shape: irregular/organic boundary vs. solar's characteristic straight-edged rectangular blocks; wrong scale: ~1 km vs. thousands of acres expected for 602 MW + BESS).

This does NOT mean the project is paper-only: TCEQ construction-stormwater NOIs for 'CLEAR FORK CREEK SOLAR' (main array, EPC Hanwha Q Cells) and 'CLEAR FORK CREEK SOLAR SUBSTATION' have been ACTIVE since 2025-08-15 and 2025-01-13 respectively -- these are real regulatory filings tied to an actual EPC, not aggregator noise. Two honest possibilities remain open: (a) ground-disturbing earthwork has not yet reached a Sentinel-2-visible scale as of the latest available low-cloud scene (2026-07-09), or (b) the true array core sits somewhat outside the ~12km search radius from the address anchor (a large ranch-land project's mapped/permitted entrance need not be at the array's visual center). Neither imagery nor a Ch.312/313/JETI boundary map (all checked, negative) can currently resolve which.

EIA-860M status field (as of last snapshot): 'under construction <=50%' -- an independent EIA report consistent with construction having started, but EIA status categories are coarse (self-reported by the entity) and do not by themselves prove Sentinel-2-visible grading exists yet.

Verdict implication: `real_active` (implying materially advanced, visually-confirmable construction) is NOT supported by imagery at the best-available site anchor. Downgraded to `real_early` -- the paper trail (signed IA 2021, financial security posted, FID Jul 2025, Meta 100% PPA, active EPC-named stormwater permits) is strong and unambiguous, but visually-confirmed construction progress is not.
construction.zone_wide_check: 2026-07-21: 12x10km frames centered on the Hwy-87 address anchor (29.2579,-97.8057), sized to cover the entire ~6,100-ac reinvestment zone from the 2025-07-14 county agenda ('generally north and south of Hwy 87, Precinct 4') whichever way it extends. 2026-07-19 (S2C_14RPT, 29.6% cloud, site readable) vs 2024-07-04 baseline (S2B_14RPT, 26.2%): agriculture/rangeland + center-pivot circles + one pre-existing tank yard on the highway, NO grading/laydown/racking anywhere in the corridor. Nixon town sits ~4.5km ENE in-frame — the original EIA 'Nixon centroid' pin was only ~4km off; construction still not visually started as of 2026-07-19.

cod_assessment.rationale: Enbridge (FID Jul 2025) states in-service 'summer of 2027'. TCEQ stormwater NOIs show site-prep/construction permits ACTIVE since Aug 2025, but no Sentinel-2-visible grading was found at the re-derived true site as of 2026-07-09 (see construction notes) -- so the visual-progress cross-check that would normally corroborate an on-track construction schedule is currently unavailable, which is why drift risk is nudged from 'med' to 'med-high' this pass. CPS Energy TSP switchyard (T-0313) scheduled complete Jan 31, 2027 (0% done as of Nov 2024) remains on the critical path regardless of array-side progress. EIA-860M candidate planned COD 2027-03. Queue COD 2027-04-29 is plausible but Enbridge's 'summer 2027' language suggests mid-year or later. Queue history shows 6 prior slips over 4 years. Project remains real and well-financed (FID, Meta PPA, $900M capex, active EPC-named permits) but the independent construction-progress evidence base is thinner than the prior pass claimed.
